content:
The test image shows a very young soybean seedling at cotyledon stage in wet/muddy soil. Key observations:
- Seedling appears to be struggling to emerge, with one collapsed/dead seedling visible to the right
- Browning/decay visible at the hypocotyl (stem near soil line)
- Wet soil conditions
- Very early growth stage — classic damping-off scenario

This points to Pythium damping-off, Rhizoctonia, or Phytophthora. Let me check reference images.

The Pythium_damping_off reference images match almost exactly — same setting: very young seedlings at cotyledon stage in wet muddy soil, with one seedling collapsed/failing to emerge and browning at the hypocotyl. The Rhizoctonia reference shows reddish-brown cankers on more mature stems. Phytophthora shows wilting of larger plants.

Let me view a couple more references to confirm.

The alternatives (Sudden_death_syndrome, Fusarium, Charcoal_Rot) all show symptoms on mature plants — leaf chlorosis, rotted roots on established plants — completely inconsistent with the test image.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Very young seedling at cotyledon stage in wet muddy soil — classic pre/post-emergence damping-off context
- One seedling collapsed/dead next to struggling seedling
- Browning at the hypocotyl near the soil line
- The Pythium_damping_off reference images are a near-identical match in both plant stage and visual appearance
